For which of the following situations can the distribution of the sample proportion $p^(^)$ be approximated as
$p^(^)∼N(p, (p(1 - p))/(n))$,
where $p$ is the population proportion?

1. A sample from a class of $24$ students, where $10%$ of the students in the school are right-handed.
2. A sample of $120$ company employees, where $60%$ of the company employees are right-handed.
3. A sample of $35$ players in a team, $70%$ of the players in the league are right-handed.

*Hint: In each case, you may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.*

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.

For which of the following situations can the distribution of the sample proportion $p^(^)$ be approximated as

$p^(^)∼N(p, (p(1 - p))/(n))$,
where $p$ is the population proportion?

1. A sample of size $n = 16$ from a population of size $N = 100$ in which $25%$ of the population has a particular characteristic.
2. A sample of size $n = 32$ from a population of size $N = 1000$ in which $10%$ of the population has a particular characteristic.
3. A sample of size $n = 32$ from a population of size $N = 1000$ in which $75%$ of the population has a particular characteristic.

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.

:knowledge-point/title: Identifying Situations When the CLT for Proportions is Appropriate
